spots.name: Australian War Memorial
spots.summary: The Australian War Memorial (AWM) is a national war memorial, museum and archive dedicated to all Australians who have died as a result of war, including peacekeeping duties. The AWM is located in Campbell, a suburb of the Australian capital city of Canberra. The grounds include five buildings and a sculpture garden.

names.ja: オーストラリア戦争記念館

spots.name: Parliament House

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Parliament House is the meeting place of the Parliament of Australia, the legislative branch of Australia's federal tier of government. The building also houses the core of the executive, containing the cabinet room and offices of the prime minister and other federal ministers.

names.ja: オーストラリア連邦議事堂

spots.name: National Gallery of Australia
spots.summary: The National Gallery of Australia (NGA), formerly the Australian National Gallery, is the national art museum of Australia and one of the largest art museums in Australia, holding more than 166,000 works of art.

names.ja: オーストラリア国立美術館

spots.name: Lake Burley Griffin
spots.summary: Lake Burley Griffin is an artificial lake in the centre of Canberra, the capital of Australia. It was created in 1963 by the damming of the Molonglo River, which formerly ran between the city centre and Parliamentary Triangle.

names.ja: バーリー・グリフィン湖

spots.name: National Library of Australia
spots.summary: The National Library of Australia (NLA), formerly the Commonwealth National Library and Commonwealth Parliament Library, is the largest reference library in Australia, responsible under the terms of the National Library Act 1960 for "maintaining and developing a national collection of library material, including a comprehensive collection of library material relating to Australia and the Australia

names.ja: オーストラリア国立図書館

spots.name: National Museum of Australia
spots.summary: The National Museum of Australia (NMA) is a national public museum in Canberra, Capital Territory, Australia. It is operated and funded by the federal government of Australia. It was formally established by the National Museum of Australia Act 1980.

names.ja: オーストラリア国立博物館

spots.name: Old Parliament House
spots.summary: Old Parliament House, formerly known as the Provisional Parliament House, was the seat of the Parliament of Australia from 1927 to 1988. The building began operation on 9 May 1927 after Parliament's relocation from Melbourne to the new capital, Canberra.

names.ja: 旧国会議事堂

spots.name: National Film and Sound Archive
spots.summary: The National Film and Sound Archive of Australia (NFSA), based in Canberra and known as ScreenSound Australia from 1999 to 2004, is Australia's audiovisual archive, responsible for developing, preserving, maintaining, promoting, and providing access to a national collection of film, television, sound, radio, video games, new media, and related documents and artefacts.

names.de: National Film and Sound Archive of Australia
names.fr: National Film and Sound Archive of Australia

names.zh: 澳洲国立影片与声音档案馆

spots.name: Telstra Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Telstra Tower is a telecommunications tower and lookout that is situated above the summit of Black Mountain in Australia's capital city of Canberra. It is named after Australia's largest telecommunications company, Telstra.

names.ja: ブラック・マウンテン・タワー

spots.name: National Portrait Gallery
spots.summary: The National Portrait Gallery, also known as the National Portrait Gallery of Australia in Canberra is a public art gallery containing portraits of prominent Australians. It was established in 1998 and moved to its present building on King Edward Terrace in December 2008.

names.ja: オーストラリア国立肖像美術館

spots.name: Australian National Botanic Gardens
spots.summary: The Australian National Botanic Gardens (ANBG) is a heritage-listed botanical garden located in Acton, Canberra, in the Australian Capital Territory, Australia. Established in 1949, the Gardens is administered by the Australian Government's Department of Agriculture, Water and the Environment.

names.ja: オーストラリア王立ボタニック・ガーデン

spots.name: National Zoo & Aquarium
spots.summary: The National Zoo and Aquarium is a privately owned 19-hectare (47-acre) zoo and aquarium in the Australian capital city of Canberra. It is located in Yarralumla at the western end of Lake Burley Griffin, next to Scrivener Dam. A major expansion opened in May 2017, with 12 ha of open range exhibits.

names.ja: 国立動物園水族館

spots.name: Questacon
spots.summary: Questacon – The National Science and Technology Centre is a science centre in Canberra, Australia. It has more than 200 interactive exhibits related to science and technology, and is a popular location for school excursions Australia-wide.

names.ja: 国立科学技術センター

spots.name: Mount Ainslie
spots.summary: Mount Ainslie is a hill with an elevation of 843 metres (2,766 ft) AHD in the northeastern suburbs of Canberra, in the Australian Capital Territory, Australia. Mount Ainslie lies within part of the Canberra Nature Park.

names.ja: アインズリー山 (オーストラリア首都特別地域)

spots.name: Black Mountain
spots.summary: Black Mountain is a small mountain with an elevation of 812 metres (2,664 ft) AHD that is situated to the west of the Canberra central business district on the northern shore of Lake Burley Griffin, in the Australian Capital Territory of Australia.

names.ja: ブラックマウンテン (オーストラリア首都特別地域)

spots.name: Captain James Cook Memorial
spots.summary: The Captain James Cook Memorial was built by the Government of Australia to commemorate the Bicentenary of Captain James Cook's first sighting of the east coast of Australia.

names.ja: キャプテン・ジェームズ・クック・メモリアル

spots.name: Big Swoop
spots.summary: Big Swoop is a sculpture located in Petrie Plaza, Civic, Australian Capital Territory. The sculpture was funded by a grant from the City Renewal Authority. It depicts an Australian magpie pecking at a chip. The sculpture was installed in Garema Place on 16 March 2022.

spots.name: Canberra Railway Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Canberra Railway Museum is located at Kingston in the Australian Capital Territory (ACT) next to Canberra railway station on the Bombala railway line. Since 2018, Canberra Railway Museum has been the trading name of a not-for-profit company, Capital Region Heritage Rail Limited, established to run the museum.

spots.name: Hotel Kurrajong
spots.summary: Hotel Kurrajong Canberra is a heritage-listed hotel located in the Canberra suburb of Barton, in the Australian Capital Territory, close to Parliament House and important national institutions within the Parliamentary Triangle.

spots.name: St John the Baptist Church, Reid

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St John the Baptist Church is an Australian Anglican church in the Canberra suburb of Reid in the Australian Capital Territory.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St John the Baptist Church, Reid

spots.name: St. Christopher’s Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Christopher's Cathedral, officially The Cathedral of St Christopher, is the main place of Roman Catholic worship and the seat of the Archbishop of the Archdiocese of Canberra and Goulburn, in the city of Canberra, in the Australian Capital Territory, Australia.

spots.name: Canberra Museum and Gallery
spots.summary: Canberra Museum and Gallery is an art gallery and museum in Canberra, the capital of Australia. It is located in Civic Square, on London Circuit, in Civic in the centre of the city. The gallery was opened on 13 February 1998.

names.ja: キャンベラ博物館美術館
names.zh: 坎培拉博物馆暨美术馆

spots.name: ANZAC Parade
spots.summary: Anzac Parade is a major arterial road and thoroughfare in the Australian capital city of Canberra, connecting the Australian War Memorial with Constitution Avenue, Parkes Way and Lake Burley Griffin. It is used for ceremonial occasions, such as Anzac Day services, and is the site of many military memorials.

spots.name: Kemal Atatürk Memorial, Canberra
spots.summary: The Kemal Atatürk Memorial is a memorial directly opposite the Australian War Memorial on Anzac Parade, the principal memorial and ceremonial parade in Canberra, the capital of Australia.

spots.name: Glebe Park
spots.summary: Glebe Park is a public park on the eastern side of Civic, Canberra, Australia. The park is bounded by Coranderrk, Ballumbir, Akuna, and Bunda Streets, and to the south, the National Convention Centre.

spots.name: Petrie Plaza
spots.summary: Petrie Plaza is a pedestrian mall located in Civic, Australian Capital Territory, Australia, being the largest centre within the Australian Capital Territory.

spots.name: Reconciliation Place
spots.summary: Reconciliation Place is an urban landscape design in the Parliamentary Triangle Canberra, Australia dedicated to reconciliation between Australia's Indigenous peoples and the mainly European settler population. Reconciliation Place was opened by Prime Minister John Howard in 2002.

spots.name: Canberra Theatre
spots.summary: Canberra Theatre Centre (CTC), also known as the Canberra Theatre, is the Australian Capital Territory’s central performing arts venue and Australia's first performing arts centre, the first Australian Government initiated performing arts centre to be completed.

names.ja: キャンベラ劇場

spots.name: John Gorton Building
spots.summary: The John Gorton Building, also referred to as the Gorton Building and formerly the Administrative Building, is a heritage listed government office located within the Parliamentary Triangle in Canberra, Australia.

spots.name: Australian National University Classics Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Australian National University Classics Museum is a small museum in Canberra. It was established at the Australian National University (ANU) in 1962 as a teaching aid to help students in the Canberra region learn about the ancient Greek and Roman worlds.

names.es: Museo de Clásicos de la Universidad Nacional Australiana

spots.name: ACT Memorial
spots.summary: The ACT Memorial is an Australian war memorial honouring men and women associated with the Australian Capital Territory who served in a number of conflicts and peacekeeping missions throughout the world.

spots.name: City Hill
spots.summary: City Hill is a park located in Canberra, Australia, on one of the points of the Parliamentary Triangle, a feature of Walter Burley Griffin's plan for the city.

spots.name: King George V Memorial
spots.summary: The King George V Memorial has been located outside Old Parliament House, Canberra since the 1940s. Commissioned in 1936 and largely completed by 1941, it took until 1953 to officially unveil the monument due to delays to the final elements of its construction which resulted from the Second World War.

spots.name: Vietnam Forces National Memorial
spots.summary: The Australian Vietnam Forces National Memorial is on Anzac Parade, the principal ceremonial and memorial avenue in Canberra, the capital city of Australia. The memorial was dedicated on 3 October 1992.

names.fr: Mémorial national aux forces du Viet Nam

spots.name: Australian Peacekeeping Memorial
spots.summary: The Australian Peacekeeping Memorial, located at the southern end of Anzac Parade in Canberra, Australian Capital Territory, commemorates the service and sacrifice of all Australians who have served on peacekeeping or peacemaking missions around the world.

spots.name: Commonwealth Avenue Bridge
spots.summary: The Commonwealth Avenue Bridge is two parallel box girder road bridges, made of pre-stressed concrete, that carry Commonwealth Avenue across Lake Burley Griffin, and connect Parkes and City in Canberra, Australia.

spots.name: Australian National University Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Australian National University Library is part of the Australian National University in Canberra, one of the world's major research universities.

names.ja: オーストラリア国立大学図書館
names.zh: 澳大利亞國立大學圖書館

spots.name: Manuka Oval
spots.summary: Manuka Oval is an Australian rules football and cricket venue located in the Canberra suburb of Griffith. The area on which the ground is situated has been used for sport since the early 20th century, but was only enclosed in 1929.

names.ja: マヌカ・オーヴァル

spots.name: Royal Australian Air Force Memorial
spots.summary: The Royal Australian Air Force Memorial is on Anzac Parade, the principal ceremonial and memorial avenue of Canberra, the capital city of Australia.

spots.name: Korean War Memorial, Canberra
spots.summary: The Australian National Korean War Memorial is on Anzac Parade, the principal ceremonial and memorial avenue in Canberra, the national capital city of Australia, south of the Australian War Memorial. The national memorial was established on 18 April 2000.

spots.name: Rats of Tobruk Memorial
spots.summary: The Rats of Tobruk Memorial is on Anzac Parade, the principal ceremonial and memorial avenue of Canberra, Australia.

spots.name: Boer War Memorial, Canberra
spots.summary: The Boer War Memorial in Canberra, Australian Capital Territory, is on Anzac Parade on the western row of memorials near Lake Burley Griffin. This commemorates the Military history of Australia during the Second Boer War, 1899-1902.

spots.name: Robert Marsden Hope Building
spots.summary: The Robert Marsden Hope Building is a heritage listed government building and the headquarters of the Office of National Intelligence, located on the edge of the Parliamentary Triangle, Canberra, Australia.

spots.name: Canberra Glassworks

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: Canberra Glassworks is an Australian gallery and glass art studio in Canberra. The studio is open to the general public to view the glass artists working. Opened in May 2007 by Jon Stanhope, it is the largest dedicated glass studio facility in Australia.

spots.name: Royal Australian Navy Memorial
spots.summary: The Royal Australian Navy Memorial on Anzac Parade in Canberra, the national capital of Australia, honours the sailors who have served to protect the nation.

spots.name: New Zealand Memorial, Canberra
spots.summary: The New Zealand Memorial in Canberra, Australia, commemorates the relationship between New Zealand and Australia, and stands at the corner of Anzac Parade and Constitution Avenue, the former bisecting the Parliamentary Triangle and the latter forming the base of the triangle that represents the form of government in Canberra, the national capital city of Australia.

spots.name: National Police Memorial
spots.summary: Australia's National Police Memorial is in the national capital, Canberra, in King's Park on the northern shore of Lake Burley Griffin adjacent to the National Carillon on Aspen Island. It commemorates Australian police who have died on duty.

spots.name: National Rose Gardens
spots.summary: The National Rose Gardens are heritage-listed rose gardens located in Parkes, a suburb of Canberra, in the Australian Capital Territory of Australia.

spots.name: Canberra Peace Park
spots.summary: The Canberra Peace Park or Peace Park is beside Lake Burley Griffin between the lake and the National Library of Australia, in Canberra, the national capital of Australia. It is not to be confused with the Canberra-Nara Peace Park nearby.

spots.name: Mounted Memorial, Canberra
spots.summary: The Mounted Memorial, Canberra is on Anzac Parade, the principal ceremonial and memorial avenue in Canberra, the national capital city of Australia. It is a copy of a memorial that was originally constructed in Port Said in 1932 but removed in 1956; a second copy was erected at Mount Clarence, Western Australia.

spots.name: Constitution Place
spots.summary: Constitution Place is a park in Canberra, the capital of Australia. The area was named in February 1998 by Prime Minister of Australia John Howard during the course of the Fourth Constitutional Convention on the options for an Australian republic.

spots.name: Reserve Bank of Australia
spots.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia Building is a heritage-listed bank building at 20-22 London Circuit, City, Canberra, Australian Capital Territory, Australia. It was designed by Howlett and Bailey in 1962 and built from 1963 to 1965 by Civil & Civic.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Reserve Bank of Australia Building, Canberra

spots.name: Hellenic Memorial, Canberra
spots.summary: The Hellenic (Greek) Memorial is on Anzac Parade, beside the Australian War Memorial in Canberra, the national capital city of Australia.

spots.name: Australian Merchant Navy Memorial
spots.summary: The Australian Merchant Navy Memorial is a memorial honouring the Australian Merchant Navy's involvement in World War I and World War II. It is located in Kings Park, on the northern shore of Lake Burley Griffin in Canberra, the national capital city of Australia.

spots.name: Australian Service Nurses National Memorial
spots.summary: The Australian Service Nurses National Memorial is on Anzac Parade, the principal ceremonial and memorial avenue of Canberra, the capital city of Australia.

spots.name: National Gallery of Australia Research Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Gallery of Australia Research Library and Archives is the pre-eminent art library in Australia, located in Canberra.
spots.wikipediaTitle: National Gallery of Australia Research Library and Archives

spots.name: Australian Army Memorial
spots.summary: The Australian Army Memorial on Anzac Parade commemorates the service of Australian soldiers.

spots.name: ACT Heritage Library

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The ACT Heritage Library is the state library of the Australian Capital Territory (ACT). It is the heritage section of the ACT Library and Information Services. Antoinette Buchanan has been the Manager of the ACT Heritage Library since 2004.

spots.name: Magna Carta Place
spots.summary: Magna Carta Place is located in Canberra, Australia to the north-west of Old Parliament House. Centrally located in the place is a Magna Carta Monument which was provided as a gift to the people of Australia from the British Government to commemorate the centenary of Federation of Australia.

spots.name: University of Canberra Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The University of Canberra Library is the principal Library of the University of Canberra, located in Bruce, Australian Capital Territory. The Library is located in Building 8, University main campus.

spots.name: Sydney and Melbourne buildings
spots.summary: These two large buildings in the centre of Civic were the first commercially-funded buildings in Canberra, and have been important local landmarks since the 1920s. Both buildings are surrounded by loggias modelled on those of buildings in Florence, Italy. They are occupied by a mix of restaurants (most of which are quite good), nightclubs, pubs and small businesses, but much of the Sydney Building

spots.name: Australian Institute of Sport (Precinct & Visitor Centre)
spots.summary: The sprawling elite sports training campus where many of Australia’s Olympic and national champions are forged. Visitors can explore the public areas of the leafy precinct, browse the official AIS Shop, and grab a bite at the onsite cafe. The complex features 'Sportex', one of the country's leading interactive sports exhibits packed with elite athletic memorabilia and virtual simulators.

names.ja: オーストラリア国立スポーツ研究所

spots.name: Rainforest Gully
spots.summary: It's the only place where you can walk from the wet tropical north of Queensland down to the wilderness of Tasmania in just three minutes, the Rainforest Gully features a vast array of flora from many different Australian rainforests.

spots.name: High Court of Australia
spots.summary: This vast building is the home of Australia's highest court and contains a vast lobby and three main courtrooms that are open to the public. Tours are available, though restricted when the court is sitting. The building also has a cafeteria. As a matter of etiquette, when you enter or leave a courtroom in session, remember to bow.

names.ja: オーストラリア高等裁判所

spots.name: Legislative Assembly Building
spots.summary: The Australian Capital Territory Legislative Assembly Building, also known as the South Building, which although may first seem like any other "government building", the building does indeed have some educational programs, and you can make a booking if you want to visit the assembly; see the [https://www.parliament.act.gov.au/visit-and-learn website] for more details.

spots.name: Banksia Garden and Centre
spots.summary: Reflects the flora more seen in the coastal parts of mid-Western Australia, part of the Outback, and most of what is seen here requires quite a long drive from Perth. For the most part however, what you see here is much more colourful than the flora seen in the Red Centre garden. The nearby Banksia Centre is occasionally open, but not all the time.

spots.name: Tasmanian Garden
spots.summary: The flora found in this garden mostly reflects the landscapes and environments you would find in the Tasmanian Wilderness, and what would otherwise require long hikes to get to in Tasmania. Look out for water dragons here – they may be lurking around and occasionally cross the path.

spots.name: National Archives of Australia

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The renovated National Archives building has excellent public galleries. It has two permanent exhibitions and holds others from time to time. The staff are most helpful if you have a personal archival query

spots.name: Rock Garden
spots.summary: Many rocks and the flora seen is what is usually seen in a typical rock garden in urban city parks. Not much unique flora here if you're coming from other parts of Australia, but it's worth visiting if you'd like to see water dragons roaming around the pathways.

spots.name: National Capital Exhibition

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: See an exhibition about the original Burley Griffin Plan for Canberra and how the city was planned and built. Good views over Lake Burley Griffin out to the museums on the Lake's south shore.

spots.name: ANU School of Art & Design Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Exhibits a variety of post-grad artworks, in particular contemporary art.

spots.name: 10 Yards

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A stylish, dimly lit neighbourhood wine bar operating out of the architectural, mid-century Aranda shopping block. The establishment places an intense focus on strict regional sustainability, drawing ingredients directly from its own surrounding multi-tiered urban farm courtyard, beehives, and fruit orchards. It is highly celebrated for its curated list of boutique Canberra-district wines, local i

spots.name: Baker's Cut

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Focusing entirely on the enduring appeal of a classic Australian sandwich, this fast-casual outlet leans into simple, transparent ingredients and fresh regional produce. They assemble a premium range of classic deli combinations utilizing artisanal breads, accompanied by gourmet yogurt cups, mixed fruit salads, seasonal frappes, and fresh cold-pressed juices. They are also highly favored by famili

spots.name: Bar Beirut

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: This energetic venue in the heart of Garema Place is a love letter to the vibrant nightlife of Lebanon. Steered by charismatic owner Soumi, who cut his teeth in the underground club scene of Beirut, it serves up exceptional Middle Eastern mezze alongside some of the capital's most creative cocktails—including their signature cucumber and vanilla-infused Wasabi Martini. The vibe is highly social an

spots.name: Bar Rochford

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Hidden upstairs on the first floor of the iconic 1920s heritage Melbourne Building, this acclaimed venue is a former winner of Gourmet Traveller’s Bar of the Year. Seamlessly blending industrial-chic concrete beams with stately green leather booths, the bar operates with a cool, unpretentious confidence. The exceptionally dynamic wine list focuses heavily on clean lo-fi, organic, and biodynamic pr

spots.name: Bella Vista Restaurant

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: An upscale, white-linen fixture on the Lake Ginninderra foreshore that has been serving Canberra since 1987. Owned and helmed by long-time Executive Chef Sebastiano Reggente, the restaurant pairs beautiful panoramic waterfront views with a polished menu that bridges traditional Southern Italian heritage and modern elegance. Notable menu standouts include their slow-simmered homemade lasagne, honey

spots.name: Beltana Farm Restaurant

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An architectural and culinary marvel standing proudly within a lush grove of over 800 oak and hazelnut truffle trees. Replacing the old historical estate concepts of the area, this destination restaurant centers around a magnificent double-sided fireplace constructed from regional Pialligo sandstone. The kitchen specializes in farmhouse-inspired shared plates that change seamlessly with the season

spots.name: Blue Eyes

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Upstairs overlooking Garema Place, this opulent lounge transports guests to the mid-century golden age of Frank Sinatra and old-world Hollywood glamour. The bar features a concave red-brick ceiling that creates an intimate, illicit speakeasy atmosphere, complete with glittering chandeliers, plush velvet curtains, and deep leather Chesterfield booths. It is a premier destination for champagne, clas

spots.name: Canberra Southern Cross Club Woden
spots.summary: This sprawling, modern social club is a beloved local anchor. The venue’s main bar, the Woden Central Clubhouse & Bar, features a warm double-sided fireplace surrounded by comfortable lounge chairs, pouring regional wines on tap and cold craft beers. The venue has numerous screens showing live sports, hosts a highly popular trivia night every Thursday, and offers casual dining at the leafy Patio d
spots.wikivoyageTitle: en:Canberra/Weston Creek, Molonglo Valley and Woden

spots.name: Dear Prudence

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Inside the historic colonnades of the Sydney Building, this intimate wine and aperitif bar brings a slice of European flair to the city centre. Outfitted with beautifully distressed walls, moody candlelit tables, and large arched windows, it mimics a romantic, low-key New York wine lounge. Part of the broader Verity Lane Market food hall precinct, the bar features a highly curated, weekly rotating

spots.name: Devil You Don't

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Underground in a cozy basement bunker opposite the Nishi Building courtyard in the NewActon precinct, this intimate, luxe cocktail speakeasy opened in early 2026 to replace the old High Jinks. Operated by the award-winning team behind Volstead Repeal, the moody, candlelit lounge features a blood-red and black velvet aesthetic with sleek brass accents. The mixology here is exceptional, focusing on

spots.name: Dumpling Inn Restaurant
spots.summary: An old-school, spacious neighbourhood institution hidden just outside the main Jamison shopping block. Highly celebrated by locals for its traditional Chinese comfort food and lively weekend push-cart Yum Cha service. The regular menu features extensive Cantonese and Szechuan-style staples, with standout dishes including crispy shredded Peking beef, three-cup chicken, and honey king prawns. Outfit

spots.name: Fun Time Pony

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Beneath the historic Sydney Building at 122 Alinga Street, this grungy, high-energy late-night dive bar is Canberra's ultimate rock-and-roll sanctuary. It packs in free pool tables, vintage pinball machines, and a loud, unhinged playlist of punk, indie, and rock. The venue serves as a major live gig space for local bands and touring acts, and serves up delicious New York-style pizza slices late in

spots.name: Majura Park Food Court
spots.summary: A massive 256-seat temperature-controlled indoor dining space. While predominantly anchored by popular national fast-casual franchises—including custom Mexican burritos and healthy bowls from Zambrero, fresh gourmet salads, sandwiches, and specialty barista coffee from Soul Origin, alongside various juice bars, sushi joints, and classic bakery lines—it serves as the ultimate budget-friendly and co

spots.name: Pizza Artigiana

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An exceptional neighborhood pizzeria serving strictly authentic, thin-crust Neapolitan style wood-fired pizzas. The pizzaiolos use traditional slow-fermented dough paired with premium imported Italian ingredients and local fresh produce. The venue is small, casual, and highly energetic, making it wildly popular with local families for takeaway or quick, unpretentious sit-down dinners.

spots.name: Au Lac Dickson Vegan Cuisine

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A mid-range vegan restaurant, and a rare sight in Canberra with delicious soy-based versions of everything. If you're not used to eating vegan cuisine but want to try, this place is a great place to start. Though this restaurant is in Canberra's de facto Chinatown, it's actually a Vietnamese restaurant, but there's plenty of other Southeast Asian dishes.

spots.name: Little Oink

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: A quirky, legendary pig-themed neighbourhood institution located just a short drive from the town center. Famed for its playful, vibrant decor and incredibly friendly community vibe, it serves up locally roasted beans alongside incredibly solid brunch classics. Standouts include their signature 'Oinko Burger' and decadent brioche French toast variants.

spots.name: The Tasty Hill

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: No, you're not going to be licking hills (or hill?) at this restaurant, instead, this is a Korean charcoal barbecue restaurant where you'll be licking some tasty barbecue chicken or wagyu beef (yep, a misleading name). But if you're after traditional Korean food, noodles, or soup, they do have some available; it's just not their main specialty.

spots.name: East Row Specialty Coffee

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: It's best known for its specialty coffee (well, it's in its name) with an all-day breakfast and has a decent variety for lunch — halloumi burgers, gnocchi, or barramundi. If you're just popping in for a quick drink on a hot summer day, there are some good smoothies and shakes, but the smoothies and shakes might not be as good as their coffee.

spots.name: Mr. B Pastel

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: A casual, vibrant Brazilian street food kitchen located a short walk from the Emu Bank waterfront. The menu centers entirely around authentic pastels (crispy, deep-fried filled pastry pockets), gourmet Brazilian sandubas (sandwiches), and pão de queijo (cheese bread balls). Highly popular for quick takeaway or a budget-friendly lunch.

spots.name: Brew and Brew Cafe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A cafe and a bar with lots of savoury treats and a wide range of meat and bread. À la carte breakfast and lunch are available and have an excellent, fine-picked wine selection, with a strong local emphasis. Wine is picked and only wines from the Canberra region (i.e., the ACT and the wineries in NSW near the ACT) are served.
